mc: Opens in Chrome and renders the grove with no errors.
Orbit works, but OrbitControls has no polar angle limit, so the camera can be dragged below the ground plane.
Runs smoothly on a standard laptop.
No UI, text or buttons. Orbit is the only input.
Stalk sway, canopy rustle and floating motes run from load with no input.
Low upward angle is close, but the framing differs: the hero stalks sit on the right instead of center left, and the tree mass is placed differently.
Stalk spacing and density are close to the photo.
Palette is near black with neon green. The photo’s yellow green canopy and pale gray green stalks are missing.
No path and no brushwood fence. The ground is a flat disc.
The photo has bright diffuse overcast light. The scene is underexposed and stalks read as dark silhouettes.
Node rings are visible at regular intervals on the near stalks.
Stalk thickness and height vary.
Stalks lean at slightly varied angles, not a perfect grid.
Canopy uses star shaped, maple like leaf sprites in saturated green, not narrow bamboo leaves.
Ground is a flat circle with a tinted bark texture. No soil or fallen leaves.
The floor is a 45 m disc with fog. The edge of the grove shows when orbiting out.
No dappled sunlight patches on stalks or ground.
Fog is too dark to read as depth, and there are no soft light shafts between stalks.
Upper canopy leaves glow with backlight.
Large areas between stalks crush to pure black.
Stalks are dark and uniform with a plastic highlight streak. No waxy bloom or yellowing visible.
Leaves read as backlit and light passes through them.
Ground material is bark texture, not soil, leaves or stones.
No unwanted roll. Convergence matches the upward view of the photo.
Canopy sways in the wind.
Bend increases with height, so stalks curve more at the top.
Wind is a sum of steady sine waves with no gust envelope, so the motion reads periodic.
Dust motes float through the scene.
Motion runs at real speed on a continuous clock with no visible jumps.
Stalks are procedurally varied with no obvious clones.
No popping or flicker seen while orbiting.
Leaves do not clip through the stalks.
Too dark and too saturated to pass for the photo at a glance.
